scenario: Forged or replayed webhook is believed or uses up a real event's ID
mitigation: Verified only in the connector worker, after storing; signature covers time and ID; inbox row written after the signature (ADR-027 D4)

scenario: Holder of a leaked webhook URL floods storage or delays genuine callbacks
mitigation: Size, rate and backlog limits on one atomic update; own small database pool; replace the endpoint (ADR-027 D4)
verification: tests/integration/webhooks.test.ts; limits not load tested until OPS-01

scenario: Connector or dependency sends a credential or data out of the stack
mitigation: Credential service on an internal network with no route out; gateway has no secret and one target (ADR-027 D5)

scenario: A person is told an email went or did not go when nobody knows
mitigation: Unknown is its own status; receipts say on whose word; a person's answer is recorded as theirs and sends nothing (ADR-027 D2 and D6)

scenario: Restore to before a send lets the same mail go twice
mitigation: Runbook keeps the connector worker stopped until unsettled intents are reviewed. The code does not enforce this; OPS-02 is the answer

scenario: Compromised web tier forges an attempt outcome or a person's resolution through the shared role
mitigation: Transition rules in triggers; web tier cannot unseal or send. A separate worker role is an open question for the outside review (ADR-027)
